answers.text: My little brother and drawing clothes. I want to make clothes people actually wear. Basketball matters a lot but I would still do the drawing if nobody saw it.
People think I am trying to be bossy when I have an idea. Sometimes I am! But sometimes everyone is waiting and I just want us to start. With my older cousins I barely say anything.
If I can make it my own I get into it. I stayed up finishing a jacket sketch for my friend. Copying definitions for class is harder even when I know it counts.
Usually I want more time with friends. A whole day of meeting new people is tiring though. After a tournament I like sitting with my brother and watching something without talking much.

I usually say the first idea. In a group science project I chose a plan before everyone had talked. My friend said she already had a different idea and I had to back up. I liked her idea when she explained it.
I picked art club over an extra basketball session. I wanted both but the times clashed. I said art pretty fast then worried I was letting the team down. Nobody actually said that to me.
I want to have a go first. I tried a sewing machine at school and got stuck. Once the teacher showed me how to thread it I wanted to do the rest myself.
Just the main thing and when it is due. A huge list makes me want to leave it. The gym closed last week so we played outside instead. I did forget my water because I grabbed my bag without checking.
I start fast then the middle can get boring. I left a comic half done. With the jacket I kept changing bits because it was for my friend and I wanted her to like it.
I try it and then ask someone a specific question. For a maths problem my friend showed me one step and I finished the others. A long video is usually too much at once.
Tell me the actual bit to change. A coach said my pass was late and pointed out the moment. That helped. Getting a whole speech in front of everyone makes me want to answer back.
I talk louder or make a joke. They might think I do not care. Sometimes I am embarrassed and want the attention off the mistake. I know that because I did it after losing my place in a presentation.

I say it straight away. My friend said I kept interrupting her about our science project. I said sorry and let her finish. At home with my uncle I wait because he goes on for ages and I do not want another argument.
After a bad game I wanted to practice immediately. My mum said we were going home. I drew for a bit and the next morning it did not feel as huge. I do not know if drawing was the reason.
I get people going. For a school stall I asked two friends to do signs while I arranged the table. One was annoyed because I had not asked what she wanted to do. We swapped jobs.
Being fast. Sometimes I answer before I understand the question. But with a drawing I can spend ages getting one sleeve right. It depends whether I care about that detail.
Let me explain even if you disagree. I try to do that for my brother when he gets upset. I am more patient with him than I am with people in my class.
I speed up and want to fix everything at once. At that presentation I lost my place and started talking faster. Usually I can laugh and start again, but with the class watching I rushed.
Being corrected over and over drains me. Music, drawing, my brother. This week I have two tests and I am a bit snappy. That is not every week.

I do finish important things. This makes me sound like I never finish anything. I got the jacket design done and I always collect my brother on my day. I am not sure what I want basketball to be long term.

questions.prompt: What matters most to you outside sport?
questions.followup: What would you like your life to make room for, now or later?

questions.prompt: What do people sometimes get wrong about you?
questions.followup: What would they understand better if they heard your side?

questions.prompt: What makes you want to put effort into something?
questions.followup: Tell us about something you chose to do, and something you found hard to care about.

questions.prompt: After spending time with other people, how do you usually feel?
questions.followup: Is it different with close friends and an unfamiliar group?

questions.prompt: In a group, how do you usually get involved?
questions.followup: When do you speak up, choose a direction, or leave room for someone else?

questions.prompt: When a choice is difficult, how do you decide?
questions.followup: Think of a recent choice. What mattered, and how long did you need?

questions.prompt: How do you approach something new or unfamiliar?
questions.followup: What makes you curious, and what makes you hold back?

questions.prompt: How much of a plan do you like before you start?
questions.followup: What happened the last time your plan changed?

questions.prompt: When something gets boring or difficult, what do you do?
questions.followup: Describe a time you kept going, changed your approach, or decided to stop.

questions.prompt: When you do not understand something, what do you try?
questions.followup: What happened the last time? Did another person or a tool help?

questions.prompt: What kind of feedback is easiest for you to use?
questions.followup: Describe feedback that helped, and anything that made it harder to take in.

questions.prompt: When you are upset, what might someone else notice?
questions.followup: What might they miss? Only tell us what you want to share.

questions.prompt: When you disagree with someone, what usually happens?
questions.followup: Can you remember an example, including what the other person actually said or did?

questions.prompt: After a disappointment, what helps you find your footing?
questions.followup: What happened on one occasion? It is okay if you are still figuring this out.

questions.prompt: What do you bring to a group that is useful?
questions.followup: Think of school, home, friends or sport. How do you share the work?

questions.prompt: When can one of your strengths get in your way?
questions.followup: How do you notice it, and is there a situation where it works differently?

questions.prompt: What makes you feel respected or fairly treated?
questions.followup: How do you try to offer that to someone else?

questions.prompt: What changes about you when the pressure rises?
questions.followup: Compare an ordinary situation with a difficult one. What was going on around you?

questions.prompt: What drains you, and what helps you feel like yourself again?
questions.followup: Is anything about your current week making a difference?

questions.prompt: What else should MORE understand about you?
questions.followup: Where have your answers missed the full picture? What are you still figuring out?
